fr:mainmatter.fr:p:
Fuckyou, I am a researcher in program semantics and verification.
This blog documents my scientific ideas in various topics.

A general theme is to provide unifying semantic guarantees for probabilistic programs and their associated logics. This is an ambitious project spanning different levels of abstraction. At the bottom, we have probability theory and many theorems are proven by classical analysis. This is particularly un-suitable for formal reasoning. Hence, one goal is to find a layer of axioms that separates the formal reasoning about programs and the underlying analysis obligations. I conjecture this can be done with new categorical foundations, such as Markov, QBS, Integrable Cones, Finite Valuation Approximable domains.

Next, suppose we have a good logic to reason with probabilistic programs and have implemented it. We should seek to write different statistical techniques in a programming model, so that our logic can soundly reason with their denotations. The logic can also be directly deployed to reason with programs.

Next, suppose we have a program describing some machine learning system component. Very likely, there are floating point operations in that program. Practical computers provide only an approximation to idealized operational and denotational semantics, which are formulated in ideal real numbers. Does there exist a set of rules which allows us to reason with such approximation compositionally? What are the compromises? ...
I hope to answer as many of these questions as possible in the next 3 years.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Algebraic Semantics and Categorical Characterization of Program Logics

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: There is a duality between categorical constructs and logical systems. For propositional logic, the Stone duality states an isomorphism between presentations of Boolean algebras (quotients of the free Boolean algebra of a given signature) and logical systems in that signature. For Hoare and separation logics, however, there is no such categorical account. What should such an account look like?

fr:title.text: End-to-end verified compilation of floating-point heap specifications

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: End-to-end verified compilation of floating-point heap specifications

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: Floating-point heap specification, for example in a separation logic, is a nontrivial problem. There exists logical machinery for this.
End-to-end behaviour conformance of floating point programs, ABSENT heap manipulation, is also a solved problem.

However, real-world floating-point programs obviously do not stay in local variables:they dynamically manipulate heap data structures containing floats, such as arrays and lists and trees with float. We would like to verify that the floating-point heap specifications at the source level pass to the target level.
For this week, there is progress in several directions.

Firstly, re-familiarised definitions of a \mathbb {K}-fibration, in particular the case where \mathbb {K} is a subcategory of Poset. Fibration ensures the existence and uniqueness of Cartesian liftings of morphisms in the underlying category, which is inherited by \mathbb {K}. These liftings are seen concretely as a predicate transform, which connects between predicate objects in the total category. More generally, in effectful settings, we deal with Monad liftings, of the form (\dot T, \dot \eta , \dot \mu ). The monad lifting transforms predicates into certain effectful versions. From this background, one can perform weakest precondition calculation in an effectul setting, which provides a semantic basis for Floyd-Hoare style logics. There is a general formula to build Cartesian monad liftings in the case of domain fibrations, and an associated wp operator. This is presented rather vaguely in as \tau \circ \Phi \circ f, but in more detail in the followup journal version.

Secondly, the work of John Li on a probabilistic separation logic is investigated. Understand that discrete conditioning is viewed as modal operator, and independence can be viewed as separation. In this sense, random variable is seen as resource ownership, with possibly the same underlying probability space. His recent ambition is to develop wp for free in the sense of .

Thirdly, the work of Justin Hsu on probabilistic relational Hoare logic is investigated. The workings of pRHL in constructing couplings syntactically, is understood. In addition, several examples are worked out, including equivalence of output distributions, stochastic dominance, and (more briefly) convergence. There is suspiciously no mention of a weakest precondition calculus. I wonder if such calculus can be constructed and given a categorical wp interpretation in the sense of Aguirre.

Fourthly, I started to introduce a Hoare logic for reasoning with higher-order functional invariants in probabilistic programs. The inspiration comes from a recent proof of tail bound for the CVM algorithm . Logical formulas of the form C \models \forall h\in SomeFuncSet. E[h(X)] \leq g(h), where g is some simple transformation on h. This would automatically generalize the usual Chernoff bounds; in fact judgments of this form is a realization of Cramer-Chernoff method. This would easily generalize a few useful identities in the first-order Hoare logic and its pre-expectation calculus. After this logic is introduced (including its assertion language and proof rules), a next step is to proof soundness and completeness with respect to some semantics. In particular, completeness is harder. Possible semantic models include the Schanuel topos and the BI-hyperdoctrine. They would be interesting to implement because of the probabilistic content.
